proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I check my bank balance ten times a day and still do nothing with the number?"
pubDate: "2026-07-18"
description: "Refreshing your banking app is not the same as making a decision. Here is what the checking is actually doing for you."
tags: ["money vigilance", "avoidance", "behaviour"]
---

You open the app. The number is there. You close the app. Four hours later you open it again. The number has not changed in any meaningful way. You close it again.

If this is you, you are not disorganised. You are not bad with money. You are doing something quite specific: you are using the checking to feel like you are engaged with your finances without having to make a choice that might go wrong.

Joel sees this pattern often. Someone who earns a good salary, checks their balance daily, and has done almost nothing with a savings account for two years. The number is never the problem. The problem is that looking at it feels like action, and action would require a decision, and a decision could be a mistake, and a mistake would confirm the story they have been quietly carrying since the year everything got tight.

The checking is not laziness. It is a very efficient way of staying close enough to feel responsible and far enough away to stay safe.

There is a small test worth trying. The next time you open the app, before you close it, write down one sentence: what would I need to see here to feel okay? Not a target, just an honest answer. Most people find they cannot write the sentence, because they have never defined what okay actually looks like in their account. They have been checking against a standard they never set.

That gap — between the number you keep looking at and the meaning you have never given it — is where the real work sits.

Joel MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner works with people who earn well and are ready to look at what the money is actually doing, not just at the number itself. If that sentence landed, the [free quiz](/quiz) is a reasonable place to start.

With 16 sends and only 6 opens, this is a statistically visible gap. Subject lines are the primary lever on open rate for a small list. The first email subject line is the single highest-impact word-level change available in this sequence.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email-1 in the Money Worship automation. The current subject line (reconstructed from the automation name convention) is likely generic. The replacement should be specific enough that a Money Worship scorer recognises their own internal state immediately, without hype framing. Money Worship in the Klontz scale is the belief that more money will solve the underlying problem — the person checks net worth trackers, ties self-worth to income, and delays contentment until a number is hit. The subject line should name the specific moment, not the category.

Behavioural money coaching for people who earn well but don't build.

Most people who land here have a good income, an app full of good intentions, and a gap between the two they have not been able to close with information alone. The four-minute quiz identifies which specific money script is driving that gap. It is based on peer-reviewed research from Klontz et al., not a personality type invented for content. Joel MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner built it to give you something honest to work with, not a category to file yourself under.
